CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right middle finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Hill is a 41-year-old female presenting with pain at the end of her right middle finger for approximately 4-5 days. The injury occurred when she was rear-ended in a motor vehicle accident at a four-way stop while stopped. She reports getting angry at the other driver and made an obscene gesture, striking the ceiling of her car with her right middle finger. She denies other injuries from the accident. X-ray reveals a distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other injuries reported from motor vehicle accident.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident occurred 4-5 days ago at a four-way stop. Other driver was reportedly texting and rear-ended patient's vehicle, causing minor damage to trunk.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and oriented. Right middle finger examined. Tenderness present over distal phalanx of right middle finger. Pain elicited with palpation at distal phalanx. No tenderness noted in proximal regions of finger. Remainder of exam normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger shows distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger, third digit. Patient placed in finger splint. Prescribed tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain, 8 tablets dispensed for 2 days. Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks. Tramadol confirmed safe with current digoxin use for atrial fibrillation.
